figure_candidates.label: Figure 1
figure_candidates.caption:
Fig. 1. A proposed pathway of the C13 Taxol side-chain biosynthesis. The Wrst committed step of side-chain synthesis (left column) is the conversion
of -phenylalanine to -phenylalanine by PAM. The portion derived directly from -phenylalanine is boxed in the Taxol molecule, and feeding stud-
ies suggest that the benzoate moiety attached to the C-13 side chain is also derived from -phenylalanine [8]. Approximately eight steps are involved
in the diterpene synthesis (right column) that leads to baccatin III.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 2
figure_candidates.caption:
Fig. 2. PuriWcation and heterologous expression of PAM. (A) SDS–PAGE analysis of the PAM protein puriWcation from each step of the PAM puri-
Wcation from T. chinensis outlined in Table 1. Lane A1, molecular weight markers; lane A2, crude extract, 30 g; lane A3, ammonium sulfate precip-
itation, 30 g; lane A4, Reactive Green 19 chromatography, 10 g; and lane A5, heparin-agarose chromatography, 1.5 g. The arrow denotes
location of PAM protein. (B) SDS–PAGE separation of protein lysates from recombinant E. coli, each lane contains the equivalent to 0.08 OD600 of
cells. Lane B5, molecular weight standards; lane B1, vector control (pBMS2000), 100 M IPTG; lane B2, pPAM2000, 100 M IPTG; lane B3,
pPAM2000, 10 M IPTG; and lane B4, pPAM2000, 1 M IPTG. The arrow denotes location of PAM protein.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 3
figure_candidates.caption:
Fig. 3. An alignment with PAM and PAL protein sequences. Multiple sequence alignment of the pam deduced amino acid sequence with the two
PAL proteins (pal-At, Arabidopsis thaliana Pal1 and pal-Pt, Pinus taeda Pal1) is depicted as well as a consensus sequence that shows only identical
amino acids among all three sequences. The internal peptide sequences generated during peptide sequencing are boxed in bold and the peptide used
to design the PAM-1.2 degenerate primer is labeled. The 11 conserved amino acids predicted to form the enzyme active site are numbered and indi-
cated with vertical boxes.
